qualitative.filing_summary_10k: The 10-K's MD&A covers fiscal year 2025 results for TKO, formed from UFC and WWE and expanded via the February 2025 Endeavor Asset Acquisition (IMG, On Location, PBR). Total revenue was $4,735.2 million, down 3% from 2024, driven by a 31% decline in the IMG segment (largely due to non-recurring 2024 Paris Olympics hospitality revenue) offset by growth in UFC (+7%) and WWE (+22%) revenue, the latter aided by new Netflix and ESPN media-rights agreements. Operating income rose sharply to $835.0 million from $30.9 million, partly because the prior year included a $375.0 million antitrust litigation settlement charge; net income attributable to TKO was $195.4 million versus $9.3 million in 2024.

qualitative.filing_summary_10k: For fiscal 2025 (ended January 31, 2026), Ulta Beauty reported net sales of $12.4 billion, up 9.7%, driven by a 5.4% comparable sales increase, the acquisition of Space NK, and new store openings (ending with 1,591 stores including 86 Space NK locations). Gross profit rose to 39.1% of sales, but SG&A expenses grew faster than sales, contributing to a net income decline to $1.15 billion from $1.20 billion the prior year. The filing also notes the Space NK acquisition, an equity-method loss from the Mexico joint venture, and continued share repurchases and store investment activity.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: For the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026, Ulta Beauty reported net sales of $3.04 billion, up from $2.79 billion a year earlier, with net income of $282.0 million versus $260.9 million in the prior-year quarter. For the 26-week period, net sales were $6.2 billion and net income was $622.5 million, both increased from the prior-year period. The balance sheet shows cash and equivalents of $158.5 million, short-term debt increased to $339.6 million, and total stockholders' equity of $2.64 billion as of August 1, 2026.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K, dated August 27, 2026, discloses under Item 2.02 that Ulta Beauty issued a press release announcing its consolidated financial results for the second fiscal quarter ended August 1, 2026, furnished as an exhibit to the filing. qualitative.filing_summary_10k: Welltower is a REIT focused on senior housing, wellness housing, and post-acute care real estate in the U.S., U.K., and Canada, operating through three segments: Seniors Housing Operating (78% of 2025 revenue), Triple-net (11%), and Outpatient Medical (7%). The filing describes a portfolio of 2,500+ communities, partnerships with 62 operating partners for its Seniors Housing Operating segment, use of RIDEA structures, triple-net master leases with bundling features, and various investment types including loans, construction funding, and unconsolidated joint ventures. Risk factors emphasize operator/tenant dependence, reimbursement program exposure (Medicare/Medicaid), labor cost pressures, competition for acquisitions, and REIT-specific tax and capital structure risks.

qualitative.filing_summary_10k: Walmart's Form 10-K for fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 reports net sales of $706.4 billion (up 4.7%) and consolidated net income of $22.3 billion, both increases from the prior year. Growth was driven by comparable sales gains in Walmart U.S. (4.3%) and Sam's Club U.S. (2.9%), with continued strength in eCommerce, grocery, and membership income. Operating expenses as a percentage of sales rose due to higher self-insured liability claims and a one-time PhonePe share-based compensation charge, while free cash flow increased to $14.9 billion. The filing also notes enactment of the OBBB Act tax law changes, which were not material to the effective tax rate but affected the timing of cash tax payments.
